name: tracker-plain-language-asks
goal: Prove Tracker sends tool and process questions to Chief of Staff without increasing Daniel’s Needs You list, keeps real decisions answerable, and teaches both launch paths the same plain-language rule.

evidence: The question recorded on 26vq3c used Tracker command names and asked how to apply authorized cleanup. Structured choices satisfied the CLI and the question reached Daniel. It belongs in the Chief of Staff inbox.

The CLI channel case covers missing choices, but previously omitted valid structured flags with tool jargon and process questions. Strengthen it and assert the plain-language rule on native briefs and canonical agent instructions.
At e005cab06c the original wording got exit 0 instead of exit 1. Native and canonical brief checks failed on missing plain-English guidance.
Flag lint uses the existing Chief of Staff route. Native and canonical launch instructions share the same plain-English guidance, mirrored and verified in the installed hand-launch template.

The unchanged three-file regression passed at the fix commit. The executable hub-and-spoke test on harbor-mbp-2 also showed a technical ask in Chief of Staff attention, absent from Daniel's flagged list, followed by a valid Daniel decision.
